criterion_notes.c1: The paper addresses basic sanitation universalization challenges in Bahia (primarily drinking-water supply and sewerage coverage deficits across municipalities), although municipal 2010 coverage deficits are used only as static baseline descriptors to assess public-works contract targeting rather than studying household or community access directly.
criterion_notes.c2: Passes the plain/literal broad wording of Criterion 2, but FAILS the narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type reading. Under the plain wording, the study examines an institutional and public-policy factor: the conception and intergovernmental investment allocation of the federal Growth Acceleration Program (PAC Saneamento) evaluated against the principles of the National Basic Sanitation Law (Lei nº 11.445/2007). Under the 2026-10-13 clarification, however, PAC Saneamento is a macro-economic infrastructure investment and project-financing program ('neodesenvolvimentismo' / capital-works allocation), not a rule-type legal or administrative mechanism directly governing household or community service access (such as eligibility screening, administrative burden, documentation or tenure rules, tariffs/cost recovery, enforcement/disconnection, or utility regulatory rules governing access); indeed, the authors report that official documents did not even disclose identifiable selection criteria for prioritizing municipalities. Note that plain_criterion2_decision is still 'exclude' because Criterion 4 also fails independently.
criterion_notes.c3: Contains empirical evidence based on documentary research and descriptive quantitative secondary-data analysis of 109 PAC Saneamento contracts (2007–2012) from federal/state monitoring systems (SISMOC, SIURB, SISPAC, SICONV, Sedur-BA) cross-tabulated with 2010 IBGE Census municipal indicators across all 417 municipalities in Bahia.
criterion_notes.c4: Fails Criterion 4: the paper explicitly notes that evaluations of PAC's effectiveness toward universalization goals had not been conducted, and its empirical outcomes are strictly fiscal/contractual—percentage of contracted funds allocated by subsector (water supply, sewerage, solid waste, drainage) and whether each municipality signed/received at least one PAC 1 or PAC 2 sanitation intervention contract ('municípios contemplados'/'atendidos pelo PAC')—rather than any measure of household or community water/sanitation access, connection, availability, continuity, quantity, affordability, or exclusion.
criterion_notes.c5: The unit of analysis (417 municipalities of Bahia and 109 PAC contracts signed 2007–2012), stratifying municipal indicators (2010 population, GDP per capita, Gini index, baseline coverage), contract-allocation outputs, and descriptive cross-sectional/documentary study design are clearly identifiable.
criterion_notes.c6: Full text is in Portuguese, which is directly eligible without translation under Criterion 9.

evidence_quotes.quote: Mas, até o momento, não foram realizadas avaliações sobre a efetividade do programa quanto às metas da universalização. Assim, neste estudo, busca-se estudar o PAC Saneamento na Bahia com o objetivo de analisar a sua concepção e priorização de investimentos em relação aos desafios da universalização do acesso aos serviços públicos de saneamento básico nesse Estado.

A investigação envolveu uma pesquisa documental sobre a concepção, as diretrizes e os investimentos PAC Saneamento e o estudo dos contratos firmados na Bahia. Fez-se também um estudo sobre as características dos municípios contemplados pelo programa, por meio de um conjunto de indicadores relacionados à cobertura dos serviços, ao PIB per capita, ao IDH, à população do município, entre outros.

Os dados revelam que 30% (125) dos municípios do Estado da Bahia foram contemplados pelo PAC 1 em, pelo menos, um tipo de intervenção de saneamento básico. Considerando o número de municípios atendidos por cada faixa populacional, constatou-se que a proporção de atendimento foi maior nos municípios de maior porte populacional (Tabela 1).

A concepção do PAC envolveu um conjunto de medidas legislativas, administrativas e de políticas de investimento, visando estimular o crescimento da economia do país, destinando recursos a áreas prioritárias de infraestrutura (logística, energia, transportes, habitação e saneamento, entre outras), sendo o setor energético o mais beneficiado.

Pela análise dos documentos oficiais do governo, não foi possível identificar os critérios utilizados para a priorização dos investimentos em relação aos municípios contemplados e às componentes do saneamento básico, exceto para os municípios situados na bacia hidrográfica do São Francisco, alvos de ações compensatórias em virtude do projeto de integração do rio São Francisco.

raw_response.exposure: Federal Growth Acceleration Program for basic sanitation (PAC 1, 2007–2010, and PAC 2, 2011–2014) infrastructure investment policy and prioritization across municipal characteristics (2010 population, GDP per capita, Gini index, and baseline water/sewerage deficit)
raw_response.outcome: Share and volume of contracted PAC funds across basic sanitation subsectors and municipal receipt ('atendimento'/'contemplação') of at least one PAC 1 or PAC 2 investment contract (no water or sanitation service-access outcome measured)
raw_response.population_and_sample: All 417 municipalities in the State of Bahia, Brazil, and 109 PAC Saneamento contracts signed between 2007 and 2012 managed by Sedur, Embasa, and Conder
raw_response.rationale: Excluded at full text (E03, with E04 as an independent co-ground). Applying the checklist in order: (1) While topically concerned with basic sanitation universalization in Bahia, the paper fails Criterion 2 under the 2026-10-13 narrow rule-type scope (E03): it analyzes macro-economic capital-infrastructure investment programming under Brazil's PAC Saneamento ('neodesenvolvimentismo' and subsector/municipal contract distribution) rather than a rule-type legal or administrative mechanism directly governing household or community service access, and explicitly finds no identifiable municipal prioritization rules in official documents. (2) Although the paper passes the plain/literal broad wording of Criterion 2 as an institutional/governance analysis of public sanitation investments vis-à-vis Lei nº 11.445/2007, plain_criterion2_decision is also 'exclude' because the study independently fails Criterion 4 (E04): as stated on p. 175, it does not evaluate program effectiveness on universalization or service access, reporting only contracted budget shares by subsector and which municipalities signed at least one PAC 1 or PAC 2 contract across 2010 population, GDP per capita, Gini, and baseline deficit brackets.
raw_response.study_design: Descriptive quantitative secondary-data and documentary policy analysis
